The publisher is Oxford University Press, with the journal site at academic.oup.com/bib. OUP's About page lists the journal under "Science Citation Index Expanded (SciSearch®)", "Journal Citation Reports/Science Edition", Current Contents/Life Sciences and Biotechnology Citation Index, and also under DOAJ, EMBASE and BIOSIS. Integrity checks:
- PubMed "Retracted Publication" for "Brief Bioinform"[jour]: 1 record, FGeneBERT (10.1093/bib/bbaf149, 2025). It was retracted and republished: retraction notice bbaf591, republished version bbaf592.

- Web searches of Retraction Watch and news on Clarivate holds or delistings for 2023–2026 found nothing about this journal, and no paper-mill special issues.
- The journal visibly publishes letters and critiques that challenge ML benchmark claims (for example bbag193 on HybridSP and bbag282 on the Seq2Topt dataset). This points to active post-publication scrutiny.

empirical_days_summary:
Main sample: n=20, received to accepted median 120 days (Q1 90.5, Q3 181.5, min 66, max 277, mean 141.7). 0/20 were accepted within 60 days and 7/20 (35%) within 100 days.

How I sampled:
- I pulled the PubMed records for "Brief Bioinform"[jour] with Entrez dates from 2025-06-01 to 2026-11-15 (n=1119), which give received/revised/accepted dates in their History field.
- I kept research articles: no reviews, systematic reviews, letters, comments, responses or editorials, a revised date present, and the 3 records with negative intervals dropped as data errors. That leaves n=917.
- I filtered titles with ML keywords (n=607) and drew a random sample of 20 with seed 20261115.
- For all 20, the received/revision/accepted dates printed on the OUP article page match PubMed exactly.

Whole population from PubMed:
- Research articles: n=917, median 124 days (IQR 92–168, min 27, max 626). 5.1% were accepted within 60 days and 31.5% within 100 days.
- Accepted in 2025: median 119 days (n=434). Accepted in 2026: median 129 days (n=481).
- All records including reviews and letters: median 121 days (n=1099).
- ML-titled subset: median 122 days (n=607).

Acceptance to online publication in the sample: median 28 days (range 20–46).
apc:
The journal has been fully open access since January 2024 (Volume 25), so there is no subscription or no-fee route for publishing.

- List price: the DOAJ record gives a maximum APC of USD 3,885 (DOAJ API, record updated 2026-09-17).
- OUP's own pages work out the APC with a SciPris calculator. The only fixed figure on the page ("Book review charge 3625 USD") also appears when no journal is selected, so it is not the research-article APC. I could not verify the official current list price from OUP.
- Amounts actually paid (OpenAPC, 2025, n=12): mean EUR 3,558.57, range EUR 2,698.10–4,380.39.
- Waivers: Letters to the Editor and Corrigenda are waived automatically. Waivers also come through OUP's low- and middle-income countries initiative, and discretionary waivers must be requested before acceptance.
- OUP Read and Publish agreements may cover the charge.
- Licences: CC BY or CC BY-NC.

Sources: https://academic.oup.com/bib/pages/open-access; https://doaj.org/api/search/journals/issn%3A1477-4054; https://olap.openapc.net/cube/openapc/aggregate?cut=journal_full_title:Briefings%20in%20Bioinformatics&drilldown=period
scope_summary:
Key sentences from the OUP About page (https://academic.oup.com/bib/pages/About):
- The journal is "an international, interdisciplinary journal serving researchers and educators across the life sciences".
- Its readership includes "mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, and clinicians applying their expertise to biological problems".
- It publishes "reviews, new methods, case studies, and opinion articles focused on the use of databases and analytical tools" in "contemporary genetics, molecular biology, and systems biology".
- "Articles range from introductory overviews to detailed protocols and analyses".
- Topics include "sequence analysis, genomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, structural bioinformatics, systems biology", "clinical and translational bioinformatics", "emerging technologies such as single-cell and spatial omics" and "AI/ML applications including deep learning in biomedicine".
- It emphasises "reproducibility and open science practices".

From the author guidelines: the journal is "a peer-reviewed fully open access journal publishing 6 issues per year online". It receives more than 2000 submissions a year and publishes less than a quarter of them.

Bottom line: ML methods are in scope only when they address a biological or biomedical problem with biological data.
author_guidelines:
Official page: https://academic.oup.com/bib/pages/author-guidelines (the same content as General_Instructions). WebFetch cut the page off before its "Preparing your manuscript" section. Items marked [snippet] come from search-engine snippets of that official page, and anything I could not confirm is marked UNVERIFIED.

Article types (open-access page and [snippet]):
- Reviews. The current length limit is UNVERIFIED; a 2019 issue PDF says 2000–7000 words.
- Problem Solving Protocols: 2000–7000 words, covering "development of methods based on comparison, new software, or new pipeline of existing software for solving a specific bioinformatics problem".
- Case Studies: 2000–5000 words, covering novel applications of methods, pipelines or software.
- Position/opinion articles, by invitation only.
- Letters to the Editor: 500–1000 words, a critique of a published BIB article.
- Manuscripts that exceed the limit by 1000 words or more are usually returned straight away [snippet].

Manuscript elements:
- Abstract: "short abstract, outlining the aims and subject matter" [snippet]. The numeric word limit is UNVERIFIED; one sampled 2025 article had an abstract of about 140 words.
- Key Points: 3–5 brief sentences summarising the key messages, shown at the end of the article. The page also says "up to 5" [snippet].
- Keywords: up to six [snippet].
- Highlights or graphical abstract: I found no requirement (UNVERIFIED).
- Formatting: manuscripts can be submitted without journal styling [snippet]. Reference style and Word/LaTeX templates are UNVERIFIED.
- Figures: abbreviations and symbols must be explained in the legend [snippet]. Format and resolution rules are UNVERIFIED.

Data and code:
- A data availability statement is mandatory.
- Sharing all data and software code is encouraged.
- Authors must use a repository that issues DOIs; Code Ocean, Dryad, Figshare, Harvard Dataverse, OSF and Zenodo are suggested.
- Exceptions can be requested through the editorial office.

Declarations and policies:
- All authors must disclose potential conflicts of interest at submission.
- Generative AI use must be disclosed in the cover letter and in the Methods or Acknowledgements.
- LLMs cannot be authors, and "It is not acceptable to use LLMs or related technologies to draft papers".
- The submitting author must provide an ORCID iD.
- Research must have been conducted ethically.
- The cover letter must disclose related preprints or publications.
- Manuscripts may be screened with iThenticate.
- A CRediT statement requirement is UNVERIFIED; published articles show "Conflict of interest" and "Data availability" sections.

Review process: single-anonymized peer review, typically with 3 reviewers. Submission is through ScholarOne (mc.manuscriptcentral.com/bib).

red_flags: Slow to acceptance. The verified sample (n=20) has a median of 120 days and the PubMed population of research articles (n=917) a median of 124 days. Only about 5% of articles were accepted within 60 days and about 31% within 100 days, and 2026 acceptances are slower (median 129 days).

OUP's headline figures of 8 days median to first decision and to final decision are dominated by desk decisions. They do not indicate time to acceptance, and OUP publishes no submission-to-acceptance metric.

No no-fee route since January 2024. The APC is up to USD 3,885 (DOAJ), and the 2025 amounts paid according to OpenAPC average EUR 3,559. I could not verify the official current OUP list price because it sits behind a calculator.

The scope requires a biological or biomedical problem, so domain-agnostic ML benchmarks (generic time-series or tabular suites) are likely out of scope. Conformal prediction is absent from 2024-2026 titles and abstracts.
JIF fell from 7.7 (2024) to 7.3 (2025), though the journal is still Q1 in both categories.

Minor integrity items: 1 retract-and-republish (FGeneBERT, 2025) and 3 Expressions of Concern (2022, 2024, 2026). I found no reports of a Clarivate hold or delisting, mass retractions or paper-mill activity.
SCIE status comes from the publisher's indexing list and JCR ranks. I could not read the Clarivate Master Journal List directly.

legitimacy: Long-established OUP journal; Crossref counts 21,247 DOIs. The OUP About page lists "Science Citation Index Expanded (SciSearch®)", "Science Citation Index®" and "Journal Citation Reports/Science Edition" under indexing, plus Clarivate JIF and category ranks. It is MEDLINE-indexed: PubMed records show Status="MEDLINE", CitationSubset IM, NLM ID 9808944. I could not open the Clarivate Master Journal List (the page renders by JavaScript and its API returned 404), so SCIE coverage rests on the publisher's own statement, hence YES_SECONDARY_SOURCE. Integrity checks: PubMed flags 6 records as "Retracted Publication" across the journal's whole history (articles from 2007, 2019, 2020, two from 2022, and a 2023 Expression of Concern record), and lists 2 Expressions of Concern (2023; Dec 2024 for btae617). These are isolated cases, not mass retractions. Searches of Retraction Watch and news found no paper-mill story about this journal and no Clarivate on-hold or delisting in 2023-2026. There are no guest-edited special issues; the supplements are ISMB/ECCB conference proceedings. Peer review is single-anonymized with typically 3 reviewers, pre-screening, and about 30% acceptance (author guidelines).

empirical_days_summary:
Main sample, n=20, received to accepted: median 146 days, Q1 101.5, Q3 182 (exclusive quartiles; inclusive 110.5/182), min 71, max 470, mean 162.8. 0/20 accepted within 60 days and 5/20 within 100 days.

How I sampled: I pulled every PubMed record for "Bioinformatics"[ta] with publication date 2025/06/01-2026/12/31 (1,293 records via E-utilities on 2026-11-15) and parsed their History dates. I removed ISMB/ECCB proceedings, identified as Crossref issue "Supplement_1/2", because their dates cover only the journal stage after conference review. I then title-keyword-filtered for ML/data-driven papers (n=466) and drew 20 at random with Python random.seed(20261115), so the picks were not hand-chosen. All 20 sets of Received / Revision received / Accepted dates were then checked on the OUP article pages and matched PubMed exactly. Some pages also print a separate "Editorial decision" date before "Accepted".

Full-population check, all 1,084 regular articles with received and accepted dates: median 159 days (IQR 117-217), min 33, max 856; 1.8% within 60 days and 15.4% within 100 days. Original-Paper-style abstracts: n=858, median 160. Application Notes: n=210, median 153.5. Accepted in 2025: median 164. Accepted in 2026: median 158.

Proceedings papers (n=45 with dates) had a median of 5 days, which reflects journal-stage processing only.

Acceptance to online publication in the sample: median 7 days (range 1-54).
apc: Fully gold open access since the 2023 volume, CC BY (OUP OA page https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/pages/open-access). That page lists a "Regular charge" for Original Articles, Application Notes and Reviews, but the amount is only in a JavaScript calculator, so I could not verify it on OUP's site. A third-party source (Manusights) reports USD 4,376, citing OUP charge data from mid-August 2026, before taxes. OUP lists the charge as $0 for Letters to the Editor, Editorials, Fast Track, Announcements and Supplement (proceedings) Papers. Discounts and waivers: ISCB members get 15% off ("ISCB members are entitled to a 15% discount on the open access fee", to be claimed before signing the licence); OUP's LMIC programme grants waivers; discretionary waivers must be requested before acceptance; Read and Publish agreements apply at participating institutions. There is no subscription or no-fee route for research articles.
scope_summary:
About page: Bioinformatics "publishes the highest quality scientific papers and review articles of interest to academic and industrial researchers." "Its main focus is on new developments in genome bioinformatics and computational biology." "One distinct section within the journal - Application Notes - focuses on shorter papers exploring the applications used for experiments."

Author guidelines: the journal "provides a forum for the exchange of information in the fields of computational molecular biology and genome bioinformatics", with emphasis on new algorithms and databases (paraphrase).

Submission categories: Genome analysis; Sequence analysis; Phylogenetics; Structural bioinformatics; Gene expression; Genetic and population analysis; Systems biology; Data and text mining; Databases and ontologies; Bioimage informatics.

Original Papers describe "new research developments in computational molecular biology" ("models, algorithms, software involving new methods, biological databases and network information services"). Key constraint: "Actual biological data must be used and, in appropriate cases, can be complemented with simulated data." "Only in extremely well-justified cases can simulated data alone be used instead of real data."

The journal is "a peer-reviewed fully open access journal publishing 12 issues per year online." Clarivate categories: Mathematical & Computational Biology; Biochemical Research Methods; Biotechnology & Applied Microbiology.
author_guidelines:
Source: https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/pages/author-guidelines (plus the General_Instructions and author-resource-centre pages).

ARTICLE TYPES:
- Original Papers: "Up to 7 pages; this is approx. 5,000 words. excluding figures", measured in the journal template.
- Application Notes: "Up to 4 pages; this is approx. 2,600 words or 2,000 words plus one figure". They must state Availability and Implementation, and the software must stay available for 2 years.
- Reviews: "3-8 pages; this is approx.3000-6000 words excluding figures". Mostly commissioned.
- Letters to the Editor and Conference Papers (ISMB/ECCB proceedings).

SUBMISSION FORMAT: First submission is format-free: "At first submission, Bioinformatics authors are no longer required to format their manuscript according to journal guidelines." Final files must be "either Word or LaTex files". The template download link was not visible (UNVERIFIED).

ABSTRACT: No official word limit found (UNVERIFIED; the "150 words" figure comes only from a third party). In 2025-26 PubMed records, abstracts are structured as MOTIVATION / RESULTS / AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION (original papers) or SUMMARY / AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION (application notes). Median length 190 words (p95 262), so no strict 150-word cap is evident.

NOT REQUIRED OR NOT FOUND:
- Highlights / graphical abstract: not mentioned (none required).
- Keywords: no requirement found; 1,276 of 1,293 PubMed records have no keywords.
- Reference style: not stated. Published articles use author-year citations, e.g. "(Vidal and Fields 2014)". Datasets must be cited in the reference list with DataCite minimum metadata.
- Figure rules: not found on the journal pages (UNVERIFIED).

SOFTWARE AND DATA:

PEER REVIEW: single-anonymized, typically 3 reviewers; pre-screening with desk returns; about 30% acceptance.

Scope: Original Papers must use real biological data ('Actual biological data must be used'). Generic ML methods tested only on non-biological benchmarks (UCR/UCI/OpenML, streaming concept-drift data) are likely out of scope or desk-rejected; about 30% acceptance with pre-screening.

empirical_days_summary:
Days from received to accepted: n=18, median 156, mean 181, quartiles 109-263 (Python exclusive method; the inclusive method gives 113.5-245.5), min 32, max 434. Only 3 of 18 were at or under 100 days and 2 of 18 at or under 60 days. Median time from acceptance to online publication was 3.5 days. Dropping the 2 non-ML papers leaves the median at 156. All dates were copied as printed in the 'Received; Received in revised form; Accepted; Available online' line of publisher-version PDFs.

How I sampled: ScienceDirect returned 403, and neither Crossref nor PubMed/PMC carries received or accepted dates for this journal, which I checked. So I took every publisher-version PDF of a 2025-2026 article I could find through three systematic routes, with no selection by speed:
(a) The HAL API returned all 24 full-text deposits with journalIssn 0957-4174 and a 2025-2026 date. These cover 23 unique DOIs: 14 publisher versions with dates, 8 author manuscripts with no dates, and 1 that returned 403.
(b) A Zenodo API search gave 3 eligible publisher versions. I excluded 1 that went online in 2024.
(c) Semantic Scholar repository links for 3,000 Crossref-listed 2025-2026 DOIs gave 1 eligible publisher version. I excluded 1 that went online in 2024.
Bias: the sample over-represents France-affiliated and open-access-depositing authors.
apc: Gold open access APC: USD 3,630 / EUR 3,310 / GBP 2,910 / JPY 472,740, excluding taxes. The business model is listed as 'Hybrid Open Access'. Source: Elsevier APC price list xlsx, 'Prices as of date: 05-Oct-2026', https://legacyfileshare.elsevier.com/els_com_pricing/article-publishing-charge.xlsx, linked from https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/pricing. A no-fee route exists: it is a hybrid journal, and Elsevier's pricing page says authors can publish under the subscription model at no cost. The APC waiver policy does not apply to hybrid journals. OpenAlex shows an older figure of USD 3,500.
scope_summary:
Official description, quoted from https://shop.elsevier.com/journals/expert-systems-with-applications/0957-4174:
"Expert Systems With Applications is a refereed international journal whose focus is on exchanging information relating to expert and intelligent systems applied in industry, government, and universities worldwide. The thrust of the journal is to publish original papers dealing with the design, development, testing, implementation, and/or management of expert and intelligent systems, and also to provide practical guidelines in the development and management of these systems."
The application areas listed include finance, engineering, medicine, chemistry, energy, information retrieval and others. "Papers in multi-agent systems, knowledge management, neural networks, knowledge discovery, data and text mining, multimedia mining, and genetic algorithms will also be published in the journal. The journal no longer considers papers that contain applications to military/defense systems."
Metaphor-based algorithms "are discouraged", and new nature-inspired proposals "must provide formal, mathematically grounded explanations for how they differ from established methods".
author_guidelines:
The ScienceDirect guide for authors (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/expert-systems-with-applications/publish/guide-for-authors) returned 403. Items marked "snippet" come from search-engine snippets of that page.
- Abstract: no more than 250 words; it must stand alone and avoid references (snippet).
- Highlights: required, as a separate editable file with "highlights" in the file name; 3-5 bullet points of at most 85 characters each, including spaces (snippet).
- Review process: double anonymized. The title page and the anonymized manuscript are separate files, and acknowledgements go only on the title page (snippet).
- Formatting and templates: Word files single-column; double-column layout is permitted only for LaTeX submissions (snippet). Whether ESWA's guide names the elsarticle class is UNVERIFIED.
- Keywords: must be in English (snippet); the required number is UNVERIFIED.
- Generative AI: use of generative AI tools in preparing the manuscript must be declared at submission (snippet).
- Data: a data availability statement is required at submission, and citing datasets is encouraged (snippet). It is not a mandatory open-data or open-code policy: published papers include statements such as "Data will be made available on request."
- Declarations seen in all 6 checked 2025-26 publisher PDFs: "CRediT authorship contribution statement", "Data availability" and "Declaration of competing interest".
- Reference style: APA author-year in practice, e.g. "Aizawa, A. (2003). ... Information Processing & Management, 39(1), 45-65. https://doi.org/..." with in-text "(Devlin et al., 2019)". The guide's exact wording is UNVERIFIED.
- UNVERIFIED (official page blocked): article types and word or page limits, graphical abstract rules, figure rules and ethics specifics. Third-party claims about limits conflict (for example, 9,000 words versus no fixed limit).
